description.narrative: The development objective of Competitiveness and Sector Diversification Project is to support sector governance improvements and increase competitiveness in targeted industries in Suriname. This project has three components. 1) The first component, Strengthening the mining sector governance, transparency, accountability, and administration, focuses on supporting improvements to the legal, regulatory, and institutional framework governing mining in Suriname. 2) The second component, Investment in SMEs and value chains in targeted emerging industries, seeks to address the limited firm capabilities, investment climate challenges, vulnerabilities to climate change, and infrastructure shortcomings that constrain opportunities for growth and diversification in agribusiness, tourism, and other emerging industries, especially for SMEs. It has the following subcomponents: (i) Program for Suriname's Growth Enterprises; and (ii) Improving the business environment for emerging industries and growth enterprises. 3) The third component, Project management and evaluation, aims to fund all project management, operational, monitoring and evaluation, and communication costs.
The project development objective is to support sector governance improvements and increase competitiveness in targeted industries in Suriname.

title.narrative: Consortia selected to receive matching grants

comment.narrative: The 16 group applicants selected for matching grant award in cohorts 1 through 4 represent a much larger number of beneficiary MSMEs (204). This progress represents 80% towards the end target achievement of 20 group applicants.

title.narrative: Consortia selected to receive matching grants

comment.narrative: The 16 group applicants selected for matching grant award in cohorts one through four represent a much larger number of beneficiary MSMEs (283). This progress represents 80 percent towards the end target achievement of 20 group applicants. Lower-than-expected consortium participation may have come as a result of cultural and structural hurdles to collaboration among firms in Suriname, including limited prior experience with cooperative ventures and weak sector-level coordination. This represents both a challenge and an opportunity for future programming to foster a stronger culture of business cooperation and trust along value chains.

title.narrative: Matching grant funding disbursed to beneficiaries

comment.narrative: To date, 73% of the total US$8.2 million allocated for SURGE matching grants has been disbursed to beneficiaries across all four cohorts. All cohorts have been awarded, and disbursements are proceeding in line with implementation schedules and verified milestones.

title.narrative: Matching grant funding disbursed to beneficiaries

comment.narrative: Of the US$8.2 million in matching grants awarded across all four cohorts, US$7.9 million (95.7 percent) has been disbursed to beneficiaries, of which US$6.6 million (82.2 percent) has been verified and supported by documentation. The remaining balance reflects price differences on purchased equipment and sits in the service provider's unused committed account pending final reconciliation.

Operationalization of the Innovation Lab at Anton de Kom University of Suriname continues to face procurement and coordination challenges. While a significant portion of equipment has been delivered and installed, procurement of seven key pieces of equipment and several consumables remains pending. The MEA has taken personal ownership of the activity and committed to accelerating implementation, and a procurement strategy has been agreed to expedite the acquisition process. The project will additionally finance limited refurbishment activities required for operationalization, including floor levelling, painting, and air conditioning installation, subject to World Bank prior review. The lab is expected to be finalized and operational by November 1st, 2026.

Procurement for the innovation lab has experienced delays. Smaller equipment has been received and installed, while most major equipment is expected between December 2025 and February 2026. To expedite delivery, the PIU will contract an individual company to complete remaining procurement packages. Governance arrangements are advancing (organigram and board composition defined), with the board expected by end-December 2025 and the lab manager to be hired thereafter. The lab's launch will be sequenced to occur once all equipment is installed to maintain momentum and credibility with stakeholders.

title.narrative: 5-Year Tourism Strategy for Suriname developed and operational

comment.narrative: The Value Chain Analysis and the Marketing Research & Strategy have been finalized and validated, with a prioritized list of recommended actions submitted. The Minister of Transport, Communications and Tourism will select priority actions for implementation within the remaining budget, with Terms of Reference for implementation support to be prepared by November 30, 2025. This sequencing enables targeted rollout of strategy actions within the project timeline.

title.narrative: 5-Year Tourism Strategy for Suriname developed and operational

comment.narrative: The 5-Year Tourism Strategy for Suriname is marked as complete, with the Ministry of Transport, Communication and Tourism (MTCT) selecting priority implementation activities for execution within the remaining project period. In alignment with the strategy's recommendations, two complimentary workstreams are now underway: a community-based tourism activity targeting three priority sites in Paramaribo, Wanica and Para, with an expanded scope to include community-based ecotourism in Brownsweg, and a national tourism marketing and awareness campaign built around visitor safety and digital outreach. Both activities are expected to be completed and formally handed over by the implementing consulting firms to the MTCT by November 2026.

title.narrative: Infrastructure upgraded to support Faster Payments established

comment.narrative: Following the May 2025 restructuring, the activity to upgrade the national payments infrastructure to enable fast digital payments is under implementation. Technical assistance to the Central Bank of Suriname is underway, and procurement/implementation planning for the core infrastructure upgrade has begun. Milestones and readiness indicators (system design, vendor contracting, oversight manuals, and cybersecurity protocols) are being sequenced toward a mid-2026 operational target.

title.narrative: Number of regulatory or policy reforms adopted to strengthen governance and competitiveness in targeted industries

comment.narrative: Legal consultants have been hired and commenced work on both the Secured Transactions Law and Collateral Registry and the Business and Professions Law, with a structured deliverables roadmap running through October 2026. Final legislative packages and implementation roadmaps are expected to be submitted to the MEA by October 2026. While parliamentary adoption of both laws before the December 31st, 2026, closing date remains uncertain given Parliament's September recess and October budget review, the Ministry still expects to receive complete draft legislative packages by project end, enabling continuity of the reform process beyond closure.

title.narrative: Number of regulatory or policy reforms adopted to strengthen governance and competitiveness in targeted industries

comment.narrative: The Secure Transactions Law draft has been finalized in substance and requires incorporation of final edits from the former legal expert's matrix to align with the new Civil Code; MEA will hire legal support to complete integration and finalize the law. The Business and Professions Law is advancing in Parliament, with the same legal support to assist its passage and to contribute to development of the Special Economic Zones Law. These actions aim to simplify licensing procedures at MEA and strengthen the enabling environment for MSMEs.
